summary: Henry Herbert Dodwell (1879–1946) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Lord Williams's School and St John's College (~1899–1902). He served in the Indian Educational Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History of India at SOAS (~1922–1946).

Henry Pitts Forster (1766–1815) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1783–1815) and was Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata (~1803–1815).
Henry Sullivan Jarrett (1839–1919) was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners, Calcutta (~1870–1894), succeeding Heinrich Blochmann.

Indologist Henry Thomas Colebrooke (1765–1837) studied under Citrapati. He served in the Bengal Civil Service, Fort William College (1782–1814), Sadar Diwani Adalat, and the Supreme Council of Bengal, later directing the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1837).

Herbert Franke (1914–2011) studied sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He studied at Cologne, Bonn, and Humboldt University under Erich Haenisch. He served as President of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1980–1985) and professor at Munich.

Herbert Härtel (1921–2005) worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1948–1953). He served as Director of the Museum für Asiatische Kunst (~1963–1986) and held a professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 1993–1994).
Herbert Niel Randle (1880–1973) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Librarian at the India Office (~1933–1949), a post he is also attested as holding at the India Office Library in 1973.

Herbert V. Guenther (1917–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Saskatchewan and by traditional teachers including Geshe Ngawang Nyima and Damcho Rinchen, he served as a professor at the University of Saskatchewan (~1964–1984).

Herbert Weir Smyth (1857–1937) was a linguist who studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Williams College (~1881–1882), Johns Hopkins (~1883–1885), Bryn Mawr (~1888–1901), and Harvard University (~1901–1925).

Herman Kellgren (1822–1856) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held a post at the University of Helsinki from ~1849 to 1856.
Hermann Beckh (1875–1937) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1900–1907) and subsequently held a post there from ~1908 to 1921.
Hermann Beythan (1875–1945) worked in Indology and linguistics. He pursued his studies under the traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

Hermann Brockhaus (1806–1877) was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian specialist who studied at Leipzig and under August Wilhelm Schlegel. He served as Professor Extraordinarius at Jena (1839) and Professor of East Asian Languages at Leipzig (1848, 1872–1877).

Indologist Hermann Brunnhofer (1841–1916) studied under Albrecht Weber and succeeded Franz Kielhorn. He taught at Goldingen Gymnasium (~1875–1881) and served as Titularprofessor at the University of Bern (1901–1914).
Hermann Camillo Kellner (1839–1916) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1860–1865). He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium zu Zwickau from ~1866 to 1904.

Hermann Collitz (1855–1935), a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Johanneum Lüneburg and under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen. He served as professor at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907).

Hermann Goetz (1898–1976) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. After studying at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1920–1923), he served as curator at Baroda Museum and Picture Gallery (~1939–1953) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1961–1972).

Hermann Grassmann (1809–1877) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Frederick William University Berlin. He taught at Marienstiftsgymnasium Stettin (1832–1834; 1852–1877 as professor), the Gewerbeschule (1834–1835), and Friedrich-Wilhelms-Gymnasium (1835–1852).

Hermann Hirt (1865–1936) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Freiburg and Leipzig University. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1896–1912) and the University of Giessen (~1912–1935).

Indologist and linguist Hermann Jacobi (1850–1937) studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Calcutta. He held posts at Münster (~1876–1885), Kiel (~1885–1889), Cologne, Munich, and the University of Bonn (attested 1925).
